{{Short description|Work by Archimedes}}
{{Italic title}}
[[File:A page from Archimedes' On Conoids and Spheroids.jpg|thumb|A page from Archimedes' On Conoids and Spheroids]]
'''''On Conoids and Spheroids''''' ({{langx|grc|Περὶ κωνοειδέων καὶ σφαιροειδέων}}) is a surviving work by the Greek mathematician and engineer [[Archimedes]] ({{circa}} 287 BC – {{circa}} 212 BC). Consisting of 32 [[Theorem#Terminology|propositions]], the work explores properties of and theorems related to the [[Solid geometry|solid]]s generated by revolution of [[conic section]]s about their axes, including [[paraboloid]]s, [[hyperboloid]]s, and [[spheroid]]s.<ref>{{harvcolnb| Coolidge | 1945 | p=7}}</ref> The principal result of the work is comparing the [[volume]] of any segment cut off by a plane with the volume of a [[cone]] with equal base and axis.<ref>{{cite EB1911|wstitle= Archimedes |volume= 02 | pages = 368&ndash;369; see page 369 |quote= "(3) On Conoids and Spheroids....." |last1= Heath |first1= Thomas Little |author-link= Thomas Little Heath }}</ref>

The work is addressed to Dositheus of Pelusium.
